b.x: What it is — craft, not a poster

Emotional intelligence is not being nice. It is not charm. It is not a score on an internet test. It is the capacity to treat feeling as information — in the body, in the room, in the decision — without letting it give the order. Gray feels. Gray names. Gray chooses. Whoever does not name is driven. Whoever names for the stage is a poster. Field 92 covers the self that asks for applause. This field covers the craft of reading.
DON'T

Shop-window IE becomes a weapon: reading the other to bend the other. That is not gray. It is a stage with a diploma. The craft reads so as not to be read, not to react to the interview, not to hand over the wheel. Not to drive someone else’s mouth.
Four branches, no diploma
The popular room mixed everything: motivation, leadership, charisma, ‘people skills’. The craft is narrower. Four branches. They fit a Tuesday.

01 Perceive — what the body already voted, what the other’s face did, the tone, the distance. Field 90: if the body tightened, the street already voted. Micro-expression and posture: the non-verbal fields. No stage diagnosis. One sign, watch. Two, leave.

02 Use — the feeling is data, not an order. Fear becomes caution, not a stage flight. Anger becomes a boundary, not a show. Sadness becomes a pause, not quitting. Anxiety becomes a checklist, not the Apocalypse. If the data does not become a useful action, you are feeding the story.

03 Understand — emotion has a cause, a blend and a progression. Irritation is not hate. Shame is not fear. Jealousy is fear with possession. ‘I feel bad’ is not a name. A narrow name: ‘I am angry because I was interrupted’, ‘I am afraid because the street changed course’. A narrow name lowers the alarm. A wide name (‘everything is over’) raises it.

04 Manage — not erase. Hold the wheel. Three breaths. One action. Silence. Leave. Ask for help at the clinic if the peak does not pass. Managing the other is ethics: calm the child, do not bend the adult. On a street that turned, managing the other is distance, not a speech.
Naming lowers the alarm

The body feels first. The mouth invents later. If the mouth invents ‘they are going to get me’, the alarm rises. If the mouth says ‘I am afraid, two people changed course, there is light five steps away’, the alarm fits the decision. Naming is not talk. It is a short label. Then field 12’s cycle: stop, breathe, name the fact, one action.
01 Where in the body? Chest, jaw, belly, hand.
02 What is the narrow name? Fear, anger, shame, disgust, sadness, relief.
03 What is the fact, not the story? ‘The motorcycle stopped.’ Not: ‘it is a hit.’
04 The peak passes if you do not feed the story. The story is the second fire.
05 One action. Leave, go quiet, drink water, call emergency services if the street already voted.
DO
Pocket sentence: ‘I feel X in Y because of Z. The fact is W. The action is one.’ No paragraph.
Blend and progression
Irritation → anger → hate. Cut at irritation. Anger already asks for a stage. Hate already picks a target.
Alert → fear → panic. Alert is useful. Fear asks for a fact. Panic asks for the clinic or emergency medical care if it does not pass.
Disappointment → sadness → despair. The house can hold disappointment. Despair that blocks Tuesday is not craft. It is care.
Wounded pride → shame → anger. A lot of ‘anger’ in the street is shame with volume. Naming the shame cuts the stage.
Nobody feels only one. Fear with anger is the interview. Shame with fear is the ‘I don’t want to seem rude’ that holds you. The second yes is born there. Name both. The cut gets easy.
Street and house are not the same room
In the street: perceive and leave. Do not ‘manage’ the stranger. Do not calm the interviewer. Distance, light, people, emergency numbers.
In the house: name, a pause, one true sentence. A child does not need your panic. They need a fact and a small task.
In a group: calm lowers the room without a speech. Whoever speaks loud to ‘lead’ already asked for a stage.
Online: the headline wants the tone, not the fact. IE here is refusing the tone. Field 23.
Child — a name, not a tale

Teaching IE to a child is not an emotion class. It is a short vocabulary and an adult who does not lie. ‘I am afraid and we are leaving.’ ‘You are angry. You may feel it. You may not hit.’ Do not ask the child to ‘stay calm’ while your body shouts. Their body reads yours. A small task: the torch, the shoe, a hand on the shoulder. The child-drill field beside it.
What this field refuses
It does not teach bending the other with stage empathy.
It does not teach a test, a ranking, ‘emotional IQ’, a guru.
It does not teach erasing the feeling. Erasing is the other end of the stage.
It does not replace a doctor, a psychologist, emergency medical care. Panic, despair, violence in the house: the clinic and the law.

It teaches only this: feeling is data. A narrow name. A fact. One action. In the street, distance. In the house, a true sentence. In the self, field 92. If the story rises, the alarm rises. If the name fits a line, the wheel comes back.
